title: Kuchela and Krishna: The Story of a Handful of Poha and True Friendship
intro: Kuchela, also called Sudama, was Krishna's childhood friend. His story from the Bhagavata Purana is short, but it says a lot about friendship, money and humility. Here it is in simple words.

p: Kuchela was a poor Brahmin who studied with Krishna and Balarama in the ashram of Sage Sandipani. The two boys became close friends there, even sharing the daily chore of collecting firewood from the forest.

After their studies Krishna became the king of Dwaraka. Kuchela stayed in his village, living simply. His family grew, but his income did not, and some days there was barely enough food for the children.

One day Kuchela's wife said, "Your friend Krishna is the king of Dwaraka. Go and meet him. He will surely help." Kuchela hesitated. How could he ask a king for help after so many years? But seeing his hungry children, he finally agreed to go.
She borrowed a little flattened rice (poha, called atukulu in Telugu) from a neighbour, tied it in a torn piece of cloth and gave it to him as a gift for his friend.

At the palace gates the guards stopped this poorly dressed visitor. But when Krishna heard the name Kuchela he ran out himself and embraced his old friend. He seated him on his own throne, washed his feet and had Queen Rukmini fan him.
Even as a king, Krishna had not forgotten the friend of his student days.

Smiling, Krishna asked, "What have you brought for me?" Kuchela felt embarrassed about his small bundle. Krishna took it, ate a handful with great delight and reached for a second. In the traditional telling Rukmini gently stopped him before a third.
Kuchela spent the day as a guest. When he left he had not asked for anything. He walked home wondering how he would face his family empty handed.

Where his hut had stood there was now a beautiful house, with enough wealth for his family. Krishna had given without being asked. Kuchela stayed humble and kept remembering God even after his fortunes changed.
Real friendship does not depend on status or wealth.
What matters is the love behind a gift, not its price. A handful of poha pleased Krishna more than any treasure.
It is fine to seek help when you are in need, and it is wise to stay humble when things improve.

faq.a: Kuchela is also known as Sudama in many traditions.

faq.q: Where is the Kuchela story told?
faq.a: It appears in the tenth canto of the Srimad Bhagavatam.
